struct CargoToml {

 #[serde(rename = "build-dependencies", default)] build_dependencies: BTreeMap<String, DependencySpec>,
 #[serde(default)] target: BTreeMap<String, TargetSection>,
 #[serde(default)] features: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,

 #[serde(default)] bench: Vec<TargetTable>,
}
struct Package {
 name: Option<String>, version: Option<String>, edition: Option<String>, license: Option<String>,
 description: Option<String>, repository: Option<String>, homepage: Option<String>, workspace: Option<String>,
 #[serde(default)] authors: Vec<String>, #[serde(default)] keywords: Vec<String>, #[serde(default)] categories: Vec<String>,
}
struct Workspace { #[serde(default)] members: Vec<String>, #[serde(default)] default_members: Vec<String>, #[serde(rename = "dependencies", default)] dependencies: BTreeMap<String, DependencySpec> }
struct TargetSection { #[serde(default)] dependencies: BTreeMap<String, DependencySpec>, #[serde(rename = "dev-dependencies", default)] dev_dependencies: BTreeMap<String, DependencySpec>, #[serde(rename = "build-dependencies", default)] build_dependencies: BTreeMap<String, DependencySpec> }
struct TargetTable { name: Option<String>, path: Option<String> }
#[serde(untagged)] enum DependencySpec { Version(String), Detailed(BTreeMap<String, toml::Value>) }
```

Helpers:
- `fn requirement(spec: &DependencySpec) -> String`: Version → clone; Detailed → `map.get("version").and_then(toml::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("*").to_string()`.
- `fn build_dependency(name: String, spec: &DependencySpec, scope: DependencyScope) -> Dependency`: kind Cargo; requirement via helper; if spec is Detailed and `map.get("workspace").and_then(toml::Value::as_bool) == Some(true)` → scope overridden to `DependencyScope::Workspace`.
- `fn resolve_members(root: &Path, entries: &[String]) -> Vec<PathBuf>`: trim trailing '/'; entry ending in `/*` → read_dir(root.join(prefix)), push `<dir>/Cargo.toml` for each immediate subdir that has a Cargo.toml; else push `root.join(entry).join("Cargo.toml")` if it exists. Sort + dedup.
- `fn build_workspace_info(manifest: &CargoToml, manifest_path: &Path) -> Option<CargoWorkspace>`: root = manifest_path's parent; members = resolve_members(root, &workspace.members); if manifest has [package], append manifest_path itself to members (root package is always a member); sort+dedup. default_members = if empty → members.clone() else resolve_members(root, &default_members). dependencies = workspace.dependencies → Dependency{kind Cargo, scope Normal}.
- `fn determine_workspace(manifest: &CargoToml, manifest_path: &Path) -> (bool, Option<PathBuf>)`:
 1. [package].workspace = "path" set → (true, dir-of canonicalize(parent.join(path).join("Cargo.toml")) fallback parent.join(path)).
 2. Else [workspace] declared → (true, parent dir).
 3. Else walk ancestors (skip own dir): for each ancestor dir whose Cargo.toml parses to a CargoToml with [workspace], resolve members and if canonicalized manifest_path is among canonicalized member paths → (true, that dir). Stop at fs root.
 4. Else (false, None).
- `fn collect_targets(manifest: &CargoToml, package_dir: &Path, package_name: &str) -> CargoTargets`: declared lib table / bin|example|test|bench arrays → CargoTarget { name: table.name.unwrap_or_default(), path: table.path.as_ref().map(PathBuf::from) }; when none declared for a kind, infer: lib `src/lib.rs` → name package_name.replace('-', "_"), path "src/lib.rs"; bins `src/main.rs` (same naming) + each top-level `*.rs` in `src/bin/` → stem name, path "src/bin/<file>"; examples/tests/benches: each top-level `*.rs` in `examples/`|`tests/`|`benches/` → stem name, relative path. Generic helper `fn infer_rs_files(dir: &Path) -> Vec<CargoTarget>`.

Populate CargoPackage fully (name default "" for virtual manifests; all Option fields from package; authors/keywords/categories default empty; dependencies Normal / dev Development / build Build; target_dependencies from all target sections' dependencies(dev|build); features = keys; default_features = features["default"] or empty; workspace_info = Some iff [workspace] declared; workspace + workspace_root from determine_workspace).

# Mission
Build the foundation of DKV's knowledge acquisition pipeline.
This milestone establishes the abstractions that every documentation source will implement.
Do **NOT** implement AI.
Do **NOT** implement RAG.
Do **NOT** implement embeddings.
Do **NOT** implement indexing.
Do **NOT** implement search.
Do **NOT** redesign existing modules.
---
# Objective
Transform DKV from
Project Scanner
↓
Project Manifest
into
Project Manifest
↓
Knowledge Providers
↓
Knowledge Documents
---
# Architecture
Introduce a new module:
```text src/providers/ ```
Suggested structure:
```text providers/ mod.rs traits.rs types.rs
cargo/ mod.rs
npm/ mod.rs
github/ mod.rs
zeal/ mod.rs
man/ mod.rs
local/ mod.rs ```
Only Cargo and Local providers should be functional in this milestone.
The others are skeletons implementing the common interfaces.
---
# Core Types
Design stable domain models.
Examples:
```rust PackageId
PackageKind
KnowledgeDocument
KnowledgeAsset
KnowledgeSource
CollectedDocs
ProviderCapabilities
ProviderMetadata ```
These models must be provider-agnostic.
No Cargo-specific or npm-specific assumptions.
---
# Provider Trait
Define the common interface.
Example:
```rust pub trait Provider { fn id(&self) -> &'static str;
fn supports(&self, package: &PackageId) -> bool;
fn capabilities(&self) -> ProviderCapabilities;
fn collect( &self, package: &PackageId, ) -> Result<CollectedDocs>; } ```
Every provider must implement this trait.
---
# Cargo Provider
Implement the first real provider.
Collect only **local** knowledge.
Supported sources:
* README.md * CHANGELOG.md * LICENSE * examples/ * benches/ * tests/ * docs/ * src/lib.rs module documentation * package metadata
Do **not** access the network.
Do **not** download docs.rs.
Return structured `CollectedDocs`.
---
# Local Provider
Implement a generic filesystem provider.
Collect:
* Markdown * AsciiDoc * HTML * Text files * PDFs (metadata only for now)
Supported extensions:
```text md markdown adoc txt rst html htm pdf ```
No parsing yet.
Just collect metadata and locations.
---
# Knowledge Model
Each document should contain metadata similar to:
```text Title Source Path Package Language Document Type Mime Type Checksum Size Last Modified Tags ```
Design this for future indexing.
---
# Provider Registry
Implement a registry responsible for:
* registering providers * discovering providers * selecting providers * dispatching collection
The scanner must not know about individual providers.
---
# CLI
Add:
```bash dkv providers ```
Example:
```text Registered Providers
cargo local github (planned) npm (planned) zeal (planned) man (planned) ```
---
# Tests
Add tests for:
* provider registry * provider selection * cargo provider * local provider * metadata generation * capability detection
Target meaningful coverage rather than arbitrary percentages.
---
# Performance
Avoid duplicate filesystem traversal.
Reuse scanner results.
Minimize allocations.
Do not read file contents unless required.
---
# Non-Goals
This milestone must **not** implement:
* docs.rs downloads * npm registry access * GitHub API access * Zeal integration * SQLite * Tantivy * Search * AI * Embeddings * RAG
Those belong to later milestones.
---
# Quality Gate
The milestone is complete only if:
```bash cargo fmt --check
cargo check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test
cargo doc --no-deps ```
all pass without warnings.
---
# Deliverables
At completion provide:
1. Architecture summary 2. New modules 3. Public APIs 4. Provider trait 5. Knowledge model 6. Cargo provider capabilities 7. Local provider capabilities 8. Test summary 9. Remaining work before Phase 3
Stop after Phase 2 foundation is complete.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::SystemTime;

/// Kind of package a knowledge provider can operate on.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum PackageKind {
 /// Cargo/Rust package.
 Cargo,
 /// Node.js package.
 Node,
 /// Arbitrary local directory (no ecosystem).
 Local,
 /// Anything else.
 Other,
}

/// Identifies a package independently of any provider.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct PackageId {
 pub kind: PackageKind,
 pub name: String,
 pub version: Option<String>,
 /// Filesystem root of the package.
 pub root: PathBuf,
}

impl PackageId {
 /// Creates a new package id without a version.
 #[must_use]
 pub fn new(kind: PackageKind, name: impl Into<String>, root: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self;
 /// Sets the version (builder-style).
 #[must_use]
 pub fn with_version(mut self, version: impl Into<String>) -> Self;
}
```

Two free functions in types.rs:

```rust
/// FNV-1a 64-bit hash (std-only; deterministic across runs).
#[must_use]
pub fn fnv1a(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
 let mut hash: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
 for &byte in bytes {
 hash ^= u64::from(byte);
 hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01b3);
 }
 hash
}

/// Lowercase hex fingerprint used for `checksum` fields.
///
/// Content-based when content was read; otherwise a metadata fingerprint over
/// the relative path, size, and last-modified nanos (deterministic, no file read).
#[must_use]
pub fn fingerprint(relative_path: &Path, size: u64, modified: &SystemTime) -> String;

/// MIME type for a file path by extension, or `None` for unknown.
/// Map: md/markdown -> "text/markdown", adoc -> "text/asciidoc", txt -> "text/plain",
/// rst -> "text/x-rst", html/htm -> "text/html", pdf -> "application/pdf", rs -> "text/x-rust",
/// toml -> "application/toml". Extension matching is lowercase and case-insensitive.
#[must_use]
pub fn mime_type_for(path: &Path) -> Option<String>;
```

Implement `fingerprint` as: build a byte buffer = relative path as bytes, then size as little-endian u64, then modified duration-since-UNIX_EPOCH nanos as little-endian u64; `fnv1a` over the whole buffer; format `{:016x}`. Handle `modified.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)` being `Err` by using Duration::ZERO (no unwrap). `fingerprint` needs `use std::time::UNIX_EPOCH` — return the hex string.

use crate::error::Result;
use crate::providers::types::{CollectedDocs, PackageId, ProviderCapabilities, ProviderMetadata};

/// Common interface implemented by every knowledge provider.
pub trait Provider {
 /// Stable unique identifier (e.g. "cargo").
 fn id(&self) -> &'static str;
 /// Display metadata for registry/CLI listing.
 fn metadata(&self) -> ProviderMetadata;
 /// Whether this provider can process the package.
 fn supports(&self, package: &PackageId) -> bool;
 /// Declared capabilities.
 fn capabilities(&self) -> ProviderCapabilities;
 /// Collect knowledge documents for the package.
 ///
 /// # Errors
 ///
 /// Returns [`crate::error::DkvError`] when the package root cannot be read.
 fn collect(&self, package: &PackageId) -> Result<CollectedDocs>;
}
```

Note: `Result` is `crate::error::Result` = `std::result::Result<T, DkvError>`.

## registry.rs — exact contract

```rust
use crate::error::{DkvError, Result};
use crate::providers::traits::Provider;
use crate::providers::types::{CollectedDocs, PackageId};

/// Holds registered providers and dispatches collection.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Registry {
 providers: Vec<Box<dyn Provider>>,
}

impl Registry {
 /// Registry with all built-in providers registered, in this exact order:
 /// cargo, local, github, npm, zeal, man (matches the `dkv providers` CLI output).
 #[must_use]
 pub fn builtin() -> Self;

 /// Registers a provider. Returns `&mut self` for chaining.
 pub fn register(&mut self, provider: Box<dyn Provider>) -> &mut Self;

 /// All registered providers, in registration order.
 #[must_use]
 pub fn providers(&self) -> &[Box<dyn Provider>];

 /// Finds a provider by id.
 #[must_use]
 pub fn find(&self, id: &str) -> Option<&dyn Provider>;

 /// Providers that `supports()` the package (selection).
 #[must_use]
 pub fn for_package(&self, package: &PackageId) -> Vec<&dyn Provider>;

 /// Collects from every provider that supports the package, returning one
 /// `CollectedDocs` per supporting provider (empty if none).
 ///
 /// # Errors
 ///
 /// Returns the first provider error encountered; errors are NOT swallowed.
 pub fn collect_all(&self, package: &PackageId) -> Result<Vec<CollectedDocs>>;

 /// Collects from a single provider by id.
 ///
 /// # Errors
 ///
 /// Returns [`DkvError::Message`] if no provider has that id, or the
 /// provider's own error.
 pub fn collect_from(&self, id: &str, package: &PackageId) -> Result<CollectedDocs>;
}
```

`collect_all` error message style: `DkvError::Message(format!("no provider registered: {id}"))` for collect_from's missing id. Preserve provider errors unchanged.

## The contract (already in place — implement against it)
`crate::providers::types` provides: `PackageId { kind, name, version: Option<String>, root: PathBuf }`, `PackageKind::Local`, `KnowledgeSource` (Documentation etc.; `as_tag()` -> "docs" for Documentation), `KnowledgeDocument { title, source, path (PathBuf, RELATIVE to root), package, language: Option<String>, mime_type, size: u64, checksum: String, modified: SystemTime, tags: Vec<String>, content: Option<String> }`, `CollectedDocs { provider: String, documents, assets }` (has Default). Free fns: `fingerprint(relative_path: &Path, size: u64, modified: &SystemTime) -> String` (deterministic, content-independent) and `mime_type_for(path: &Path) -> Option<String>` (md/markdown->"text/markdown", adoc->"text/asciidoc", txt->"text/plain", rst->"text/x-rst", html/htm->"text/html", pdf->"application/pdf"; case-insensitive). `crate::error::Result` = Result<T, DkvError>; `DkvError::Io(#[from] io::Error)` so `?` on fs/walkdir errors works.

The current file has `pub struct LocalProvider;` with `impl Provider` (id "local", metadata, supports: kind==Local, capabilities: offline true, kinds [Local], sources [Documentation], reads_content false) and a stub `collect` returning empty. KEEP the struct, metadata, supports, capabilities EXACTLY. Replace only the `collect` body and add private helpers + unit tests.

## What `collect` must do (metadata + locations ONLY — no content parsing, no file-content reads)
Given `package: &PackageId` with `root = package.root`:

1. **Root validation**: `fs::metadata(&package.root)` — propagate errors with `?`; if not a directory, return an Io error (construct via `fs::metadata` on a nonexistent path is naturally an error; simplest: `let meta = fs::metadata(&package.root)?; if !meta.is_dir() { return Err(DkvError::Io(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotADirectory, "package root is not a directory"))); }` — you may need `use std::io;`).

2. **Walk**: `walkdir::WalkDir::new(&package.root).follow_links(false)` recursively. For each entry:
 - Skip the root itself.
 - Skip any entry whose file name starts with `.` (hidden files AND hidden directories — do not descend into `.git`, `.hidden/`, etc.).
 - Keep only regular files (`entry.file_type().is_file()`; note `DirEntry::file_type()` requires `entry.file_type()` not `entry.metadata()`).
 - Accept only extensions in: `md`, `markdown`, `adoc`, `txt`, `rst`, `html`, `htm`, `pdf` — case-insensitive (`.MD` works). Everything else is skipped.
 - For accepted files emit a `KnowledgeDocument`:
 - title = file stem (e.g. `guide` for `guide.adoc`; use `Path::file_stem`, fall back to full file name via `map_or_else` if stem is None)
 - source = `KnowledgeSource::Documentation`, path = path relative to root (strip the root prefix; use `path.strip_prefix(&package.root)` via `map_err`/`ok_or_else` — it must succeed since walkdir starts at root)
 - package = `package.name.clone()`, language = None (docs, not code), mime = `mime_type_for(&path).unwrap_or_else(|| "application/octet-stream".to_string())`
 - size + modified from `entry.metadata()?` (modified via `.modified()` — if it errors use `SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH` via `unwrap_or`/`unwrap_or_default`-style handling, no unwrap)
 - checksum = `fingerprint(&relative_path, size, &modified)`
 - tags = `vec!["docs".to_string()]` — actually use `KnowledgeSource::Documentation.as_tag().to_string()` (returns "docs")
 - content = None (metadata only — this is the "PDFs metadata-only" and "no parsing yet" requirement; PDFs are documents here too, mime application/pdf, content None)

3. **Determinism**: collect into a Vec, sort by `path`, return `Ok(CollectedDocs { provider: self.id().to_string(), documents, assets: Vec::new() })`. Empty dir -> Ok(empty). Missing root -> Err (Io).

1. **Errors**: storage/errors.rs → `StorageError` (thiserror): Io(#[from] io::Error), Sqlite(#[from] rusqlite::Error), Migration(String), NotFound(String), InvalidLayout(String), Message(String) + storage-local `Result<T>`. Add `DkvError::Storage(#[from] StorageError)` to error.rs.

pub enum StorageError {
 #[error(transparent)] Io(#[from] std::io::Error),

}

//! Module docs describing the storage layer: providers produce `CollectedDocs`;
//! storage normalizes, deduplicates, and persists them into a vault backed by
//! SQLite. The trait below keeps storage independent of the backend: SQLite is
//! the first backend; the trait exists so tests and future backends (or
//! export/import) do not change the ingest pipeline.

mod checksum;
mod errors;
mod layout;
mod metadata;
// NOTE: sqlite, transaction, vault, ingest are declared here as modules too;
// their files currently contain only module docs (stubs filled by later lanes).

pub mod sqlite;
pub mod transaction;
pub mod vault;
pub mod ingest;

pub use checksum::{ChecksumKind, content_checksum, content_checksum_file};
pub use errors::{Result, StorageError};
pub use layout::VaultLayout;
pub use metadata::{
 ArtifactRecord, ChecksumRecord, Counts, DocumentRecord, IngestReport, IngestRunRecord,
 PackageKey, PackageRecord, PendingArtifact, PendingBatch, PendingDocument, SourceRecord,
 StatusReport, TagRecord, VerifyReport,
};

use std::path::Path;
use crate::providers::types::PackageId; // no: see below

/// Storage backend abstraction: SQLite is the first implementation.
pub trait StorageBackend: Send {
 /// Opens (or creates) the database at `path`. Callers must call
 /// [`StorageBackend::migrate`] after opening before any other method.
 /// `Self: Sized` — used through concrete backends; `Vault::open` boxes a
 /// concrete backend.
 fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<Self>
 where
 Self: Sized;

 /// Applies pending schema migrations (idempotent; guarded by `PRAGMA user_version`).
 fn migrate(&mut self) -> Result<()>;

 /// Persists one normalized batch atomically: one transaction; every row and
 /// staged content file is rolled back on any failure. Content files are
 /// staged under `layout.tmp_dir()`, then renamed to `layout.documents_dir()/<sha256>`
 /// before commit (skip if already present). Inserts one `ingest_runs` row.
 fn ingest(&mut self, layout: &VaultLayout, batch: &PendingBatch) -> Result<IngestReport>;

 /// Row counts.
 fn counts(&self) -> Result<Counts>;

 /// Total bytes of stored document content (sum over `checksums.size` for
 /// content stored in the vault; never raw source sizes).
 fn storage_size(&self) -> Result<u64>;

 /// Verifies stored content against the on-disk vault (missing files,
 /// checksum mismatches, orphaned rows, reverse orphans). Read-only.
 fn verify(&self, layout: &VaultLayout) -> Result<VerifyReport>;
}
```

```rust
//! Module docs: providers produce `CollectedDocs`; storage normalizes, deduplicates,
//! and persists them into a vault. `StorageBackend` keeps storage independent of the
//! backend: SQLite is the first backend; the trait exists so tests and future
//! backends (or export/import) do not change the ingest pipeline.

mod checksum;
mod errors;
mod layout;
mod metadata;

pub mod sqlite;
pub mod transaction;
pub mod vault;
pub mod ingest;

pub use checksum::{ChecksumKind, content_checksum, content_checksum_file};
pub use errors::{Result, StorageError};
pub use layout::VaultLayout;
pub use metadata::{
 ArtifactRecord, ChecksumRecord, Counts, DocumentRecord, IngestReport, IngestRunRecord,
 PackageKey, PackageRecord, PendingArtifact, PendingBatch, PendingDocument, SourceRecord,
 StatusReport, TagRecord, VerifyReport,
};

use std::path::Path;

/// Storage backend abstraction; SQLite is the first implementation.
pub trait StorageBackend: Send {
 /// Opens (or creates) the database at `path`. Callers must call
 /// [`StorageBackend::migrate`] after opening before any other method.
 /// `Self: Sized` — `Vault::open` boxes a concrete backend.
 fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<Self> where Self: Sized;

 /// Applies pending schema migrations (idempotent, guarded by `PRAGMA user_version`).
 fn migrate(&mut self) -> Result<()>;

 /// Persists one normalized batch atomically: one transaction; every row and
 /// staged content file is rolled back on any failure. Content files are
 /// staged under `layout.tmp_dir()`, renamed to `layout.documents_dir()/<sha256>`
 /// before commit (skip if already present). Inserts one `ingest_runs` row.
 fn ingest(&mut self, layout: &VaultLayout, batch: &PendingBatch) -> Result<IngestReport>;

 /// Row counts.
 fn counts(&self) -> Result<Counts>;

 /// Total bytes of stored document content (sum over `checksums.size` for
 /// content stored in the vault; never raw source sizes).
 fn storage_size(&self) -> Result<u64>;

 /// Verifies stored content against the on-disk vault (missing files, checksum
 /// mismatches, orphaned rows, reverse orphans). Read-only.
 fn verify(&self, layout: &VaultLayout) -> Result<VerifyReport>;
}
```

### Migrations (the "migrations from the beginning" requirement)
- `const MIGRATIONS: &[&str] = &[/* v1 schema SQL */];` — one string per version. v1 is the full schema below.
- `migrate()`: read `PRAGMA user_version` (i64); for each migration index >= version: `let tx = self.conn.transaction()?; tx.execute_batch(migration_sql)?; tx.pragma_update(None, "user_version", (i + 1) as i64)?; tx.commit()?;`. Idempotent (re-running applies nothing). Errors → `StorageError::Migration` wrapping the rusqlite error message.

### v1 schema SQL (EXACT — includes a critical dedup fix)
```sql
CREATE TABLE packages (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 kind TEXT NOT NULL,
 name TEXT NOT NULL,
 version TEXT,
 root TEXT,
 first_seen_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 last_seen_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE sources (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 provider TEXT NOT NULL,
 source TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE checksums (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 algorithm TEXT NOT NULL,
 value TEXT NOT NULL,
 size INTEGER NOT NULL,
 ref_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);
CREATE TABLE documents (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 package_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES packages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
 source_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sources(id),
 title TEXT NOT NULL,
 relative_path TEXT NOT NULL,
 fs_path TEXT,
 vault_path TEXT,
 origin_url TEXT,
 mime_type TEXT NOT NULL,
 language TEXT,
 size INTEGER NOT NULL,
 metadata_checksum TEXT NOT NULL,
 content_checksum_id INTEGER REFERENCES checksums(id),
 content_stored INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
 modified_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 ingested_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE artifacts (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 package_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES packages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
 name TEXT NOT NULL,
 source TEXT NOT NULL,
 path TEXT NOT NULL,
 fs_path TEXT,
 mime_type TEXT,
 size INTEGER NOT NULL,
 checksum TEXT NOT NULL,
 modified_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 ingested_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE tags (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
);
CREATE TABLE document_tags (
 document_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES documents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
 tag_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tags(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
 PRIMARY KEY (document_id, tag_id)
);
CREATE TABLE ingest_runs (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 started_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 finished_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 status TEXT NOT NULL,
 packages INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
 documents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
 artifacts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
 error TEXT
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_packages_identity ON packages(kind, name, COALESCE(version, ''));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_sources_identity ON sources(provider, source);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_checksums_identity ON checksums(algorithm, value);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_documents_identity ON documents(package_id, source_id, relative_path);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_artifacts_identity ON artifacts(package_id, name, path);
CREATE INDEX idx_documents_package_id ON documents(package_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_documents_source_id ON documents(source_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_documents_content_checksum_id ON documents(content_checksum_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_artifacts_package_id ON artifacts(package_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_document_tags_tag_id ON document_tags(tag_id);
```
WHY the expression index on packages: `UNIQUE(kind,name,version)` would NOT dedup version-less packages (SQLite treats NULLs as distinct in unique indexes) — re-ingesting a Local package would mint new package rows and duplicate documents. `COALESCE(version,'')` fixes that. Use it exactly.

### ingest(layout, batch) — one atomic transaction
Contract: stage content files, persist rows, insert one ingest_runs row, all-or-nothing. Algorithm:
1. `let mut tx = self.conn.transaction()?;` (wrap in `SqliteTransaction::new(tx)`).
2. `let started_at = now_epoch_secs();`
3. Stage content: for each `PendingDocument` with `content: Some(bytes)` (content_checksum is `Some(sha)` there — guaranteed by the pipeline; still handle None defensively by skipping):
 - `let staged = layout.tmp_dir().join(format!("{}-{}", started_at, idx));` (no rand dep; timestamp+index is unique enough per batch)
 - `std::fs::write(&staged, bytes)?;` track in a `created_files: Vec<PathBuf>`.
 - `let target = layout.document_file(sha);` If `target` exists: if it is a directory → return `StorageError::InvalidLayout("content target exists but is a directory".into())` (this is the deterministic failure injection used by rollback tests); else skip (content already stored — dedup across ingests). If it does not exist: `std::fs::rename(&staged, &target)?;` track `target` in `created_files`.
4. Persist (all via the SqliteTransaction wrapper, per document):
 - `package_id = upsert_package(&doc.package, started_at)` — root stored as `doc.package.root.to_string_lossy()`, version as-is (Option).
 - `source_id = upsert_source(&doc.provider, &doc.source.as_tag())`
 - if content present: `checksum_id = Some(get_or_create_checksum(sha, size_of_content_bytes))` (size = hashed byte length; algorithm "sha256")
 - `document_id = upsert_document(...)` with all fields; `content_stored = content.is_some()`, `modified_at` from `doc.modified` (epoch secs), `ingested_at = started_at`.
 - tags: for each tag name: `tag_id = upsert_tag(name)`; `link_document_tag(document_id, tag_id)`.
 - artifacts: `upsert_artifact(...)` (no tags/links for artifacts in v1).
5. `run_id = record_ingest_run(started_at, now, "ok", unique_package_count as i64, batch.documents.len() as i64, batch.artifacts.len() as i64)` — unique_package_count = distinct PackageKey values in batch (kind+name+version).
6. `tx.commit()?` → return `IngestReport { run_id, packages: unique_package_count, documents: batch.documents.len(), artifacts: batch.artifacts.len() }`.
7. On ANY error before commit: drop/rollback the transaction AND best-effort remove every path in `created_files` (`let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);` — never panic on cleanup failure), then return the error. The transaction must not commit.
- Prepared statements: use `tx.prepare_cached` where convenient; remember rusqlite `Transaction` borrows the connection mutably — do all file I/O outside the transaction's statement lifetimes (file I/O needs no connection, so sequence statements and file ops; drop statements before calling `tx.commit()`).
- Upsert patterns (return row id via `RETURNING id`):
 - packages: `INSERT INTO packages (kind,name,version,root,first_seen_at,last_seen_at) VALUES (?1,?2,?3,?4,?5,?5) ON CONFLICT(kind, name, COALESCE(version,'')) DO UPDATE SET root=excluded.root, last_seen_at=excluded.last_seen_at RETURNING id`
 - sources: `INSERT INTO sources (provider,source) VALUES (?1,?2) ON CONFLICT(provider,source) DO UPDATE SET provider=excluded.provider RETURNING id`
 - checksums: `INSERT INTO checksums (algorithm,value,size,ref_count) VALUES ('sha256',?1,?2,1) ON CONFLICT(algorithm,value) DO UPDATE SET ref_count=ref_count+1 RETURNING id`
 - documents: `INSERT INTO documents (package_id,source_id,title,relative_path,fs_path,vault_path,origin_url,mime_type,language,size,metadata_checksum,content_checksum_id,content_stored,modified_at,ingested_at) VALUES (?1..?15) ON CONFLICT(package_id, source_id, relative_path) DO UPDATE SET title=excluded.title, fs_path=excluded.fs_path, vault_path=excluded.vault_path, origin_url=excluded.origin_url, mime_type=excluded.mime_type, language=excluded.language, size=excluded.size, metadata_checksum=excluded.metadata_checksum, content_checksum_id=excluded.content_checksum_id, content_stored=excluded.content_stored, modified_at=excluded.modified_at, ingested_at=excluded.ingested_at RETURNING id`
 - artifacts: analogous with `ON CONFLICT(package_id, name, path) DO UPDATE SET ... RETURNING id`
 - tags: `INSERT INTO tags (name) VALUES (?1) ON CONFLICT(name) DO UPDATE SET name=excluded.name RETURNING id`
 - document_tags: `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO document_tags (document_id, tag_id) VALUES (?1,?2)`
 - ingest_runs: plain `INSERT INTO ingest_runs (...) VALUES (...)` + `last_insert_rowid()` or `RETURNING id`.
- NOTE: `ON CONFLICT(kind, name, COALESCE(version,''))` requires the expression index from the schema to exist (it does). If rusqlite/SQLite rejects the expression conflict target, fall back to: upsert by (kind,name,version) for versioned rows AND a second path for NULL-version rows — but try the expression form first; it is supported on the bundled SQLite.

### counts()
`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM packages;` / documents / artifacts → `Counts { ... }` (i64s).

### storage_size()
`SELECT COALESCE(SUM(c.size), 0) FROM checksums c INNER JOIN documents d ON d.content_checksum_id = c.id WHERE d.content_stored = 1;` — i64 result; convert to u64 with `u64::try_from(...).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)` (repo pattern for cast lints).

### verify(layout) — read-only, all categories are warnings
1. `missing_files`: `SELECT fs_path FROM documents WHERE fs_path IS NOT NULL;` → for each, if the path does not exist → push (PathBuf).
2. Stored docs: `SELECT d.vault_path, c.value FROM documents d JOIN checksums c ON d.content_checksum_id = c.id WHERE d.content_stored = 1;` → `checksum_mismatches`: for each, `file = layout.document_file(sha)` where `sha` = vault_path after stripping the `documents/` prefix (or parse from `c.value` — the checksum IS the filename); if the file exists and `content_checksum_file(&file)?` != `c.value` → push file. If the file exists but is a directory or unreadable → treat as mismatch (push it). `orphaned_rows`: if the file does NOT exist → push the vault_path String.
3. `reverse_orphans`: `std::fs::read_dir(layout.documents_dir())` (tolerate NotFound → empty): for each entry, if its file name is not in the set of known stored checksum values (from step 2) → push its path.
4. Sort all four vecs (deterministic output). Return `VerifyReport`.

## src/storage/ingest.rs — the pipeline (overwrite the stub)
Module docs + three public fns (signatures PINNED — downstream lanes call these):

```rust
/// Normalizes and deduplicates collected docs into one batch ready to persist.
/// Documents are keyed by (package, provider, source tag, relative path); the
/// first occurrence wins. Content documents get a SHA-256 content checksum and
/// a logical vault path; metadata-only documents carry neither.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`StorageError`] if a document's content cannot be checksummed
/// (cannot happen in practice: content is in memory) — errors are reserved for
/// future streaming paths.
pub fn normalize_batch(
 layout: &VaultLayout,
 entries: &[(PackageId, CollectedDocs)],
) -> Result<PendingBatch>

/// Ingests collected docs into the vault backend in ONE atomic transaction.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`StorageError`] if normalization or the backend ingest fails
/// (backend rolls back completely on failure).
pub fn ingest_collected(
 layout: &VaultLayout,
 backend: &mut dyn StorageBackend,
 entries: &[(PackageId, CollectedDocs)],
) -> Result<IngestReport>

/// Scans a project directory, collects knowledge from all registered
/// providers, and ingests everything into the vault.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`StorageError`] if the project cannot be detected, a provider
/// collection fails, or the ingest fails.
pub fn ingest_project(
 layout: &VaultLayout,
 backend: &mut dyn StorageBackend,
 root: &Path,
 exclusions: &[String],
) -> Result<IngestReport>
```

### normalize_batch logic
- For each `(package_id, collected)` pair:
 - documents: map each `KnowledgeDocument` → `PendingDocument`:
 - `package: PackageKey::new(package_id)`
 - `provider: collected.provider.clone()`
 - `source: doc.source`
 - `title: doc.title.clone()`
 - `relative_path: doc.path.clone()`
 - `fs_path: Some(package_id.root.join(&doc.path))`
 - `mime_type`, `language`, `size`, `metadata_checksum: doc.checksum.clone()`, `modified: doc.modified`, `tags: doc.tags.clone()` (clone)
 - `content: doc.content.clone()`
 - content fields: if `content` is Some → `content_checksum = Some(crate::storage::content_checksum(bytes))`, `vault_path = Some(layout.logical_vault_path(&sha))`; else both None.
 - `origin_url: None`
 - assets: map each `KnowledgeAsset` → `PendingArtifact` similarly (`fs_path: Some(package_id.root.join(&asset.path))`, no content fields).
- Dedup: track a `BTreeSet` of `(kind, name, version, provider, source_tag, relative_path)` — skip any document whose key is already present (first occurrence wins). Artifacts keyed by `(kind, name, version, provider, name, path)`.
- Return the batch.

### ingest_collected logic
`let batch = normalize_batch(layout, entries)?; backend.ingest(layout, &batch)` — with `backend.migrate()` NOT called here (the caller opens+migrates; do not double-migrate). Actually: call it defensively? No — document that the backend must already be migrated; just ingest.

### ingest_project logic
1. `let project = crate::project::detect::detect(root, exclusions)?;` (map its error into `StorageError` via a helper: `map_err(|e| StorageError::Message(e.to_string()))`).
2. Build `entries: Vec<(PackageId, CollectedDocs)>`:
 - for each `CargoPackage` in `project.cargo_packages`: `let pid = PackageId::from_cargo(pkg);` for each `collected` in `Registry::builtin().collect_all(&pid)?` → push `(pid.clone(), collected)`.
 - for each `NodePackage` in `project.node_packages`: `let pid = PackageId::from_node(pkg);` same loop (npm is Planned → `collect_all` returns empty; that is expected, not an error).

### v1 schema SQL (EXACT — includes a critical dedup fix)
```sql
CREATE TABLE packages (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 kind TEXT NOT NULL,
 name TEXT NOT NULL,
 version TEXT,
 root TEXT,
 first_seen_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 last_seen_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE sources (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 provider TEXT NOT NULL,
 source TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE checksums (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 algorithm TEXT NOT NULL,
 value TEXT NOT NULL,
 size INTEGER NOT NULL,
 ref_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);
CREATE TABLE documents (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 package_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES packages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
 source_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sources(id),
 title TEXT NOT NULL,
 relative_path TEXT NOT NULL,
 fs_path TEXT,
 vault_path TEXT,
 origin_url TEXT,
 mime_type TEXT NOT NULL,
 language TEXT,
 size INTEGER NOT NULL,
 metadata_checksum TEXT NOT NULL,
 content_checksum_id INTEGER REFERENCES checksums(id),
 content_stored INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
 modified_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 ingested_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE artifacts (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 package_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES packages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
 name TEXT NOT NULL,
 source TEXT NOT NULL,
 path TEXT NOT NULL,
 fs_path TEXT,
 mime_type TEXT,
 size INTEGER NOT NULL,
 checksum TEXT NOT NULL,
 modified_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 ingested_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE tags (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
);
CREATE TABLE document_tags (
 document_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES documents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
 tag_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tags(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
 PRIMARY KEY (document_id, tag_id)
);
CREATE TABLE ingest_runs (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 started_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 finished_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 status TEXT NOT NULL,
 packages INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
 documents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
 artifacts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
 error TEXT
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_packages_identity ON packages(kind, name, COALESCE(version, ''));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_sources_identity ON sources(provider, source);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_checksums_identity ON checksums(algorithm, value);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_documents_identity ON documents(package_id, source_id, relative_path);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_artifacts_identity ON artifacts(package_id, name, path);
CREATE INDEX idx_documents_package_id ON documents(package_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_documents_source_id ON documents(source_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_documents_content_checksum_id ON documents(content_checksum_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_artifacts_package_id ON artifacts(package_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_document_tags_tag_id ON document_tags(tag_id);
```
WHY the expression index on packages: `UNIQUE(kind,name,version)` would NOT dedup version-less packages (SQLite treats NULLs as distinct in unique indexes) — re-ingesting a Local package would mint new package rows and duplicate documents. `COALESCE(version,'')` fixes that. Use it exactly.

### ingest(layout, batch) — one atomic transaction
Contract: stage content files, persist rows, insert one ingest_runs row, all-or-nothing. Algorithm:
1. `let mut tx = self.conn.transaction()?;` (wrap in `SqliteTransaction::new(tx)`).
2. `let started_at = now_epoch_secs();`
3. Stage content: for each `PendingDocument` with `content: Some(bytes)` (content_checksum is `Some(sha)` there — guaranteed by the pipeline; still handle None defensively by skipping):
 - `let staged = layout.tmp_dir().join(format!("{}-{}", started_at, idx));` (no rand dep; timestamp+index is unique enough per batch)
 - `std::fs::write(&staged, bytes)?;` track in a `created_files: Vec<PathBuf>`.
 - `let target = layout.document_file(sha);` If `target` exists: if it is a directory → return `StorageError::InvalidLayout("content target exists but is a directory".into())` (this is the deterministic failure injection used by rollback tests); else skip (content already stored — dedup across ingests). If it does not exist: `std::fs::rename(&staged, &target)?;` track `target` in `created_files`.
4. Persist (all via the SqliteTransaction wrapper, per document):
 - `package_id = upsert_package(&doc.package, started_at)` — root stored as `doc.package.root.to_string_lossy()`, version as-is (Option).
 - `source_id = upsert_source(&doc.provider, &doc.source.as_tag())`
 - if content present: `checksum_id = Some(get_or_create_checksum(sha, size_of_content_bytes))` (size = hashed byte length; algorithm "sha256")
 - `document_id = upsert_document(...)` with all fields; `content_stored = content.is_some()`, `modified_at` from `doc.modified` (epoch secs), `ingested_at = started_at`.
 - tags: for each tag name: `tag_id = upsert_tag(name)`; `link_document_tag(document_id, tag_id)`.
 - artifacts: `upsert_artifact(...)` (no tags/links for artifacts in v1).
5. `run_id = record_ingest_run(started_at, now, "ok", unique_package_count as i64, batch.documents.len() as i64, batch.artifacts.len() as i64)` — unique_package_count = distinct PackageKey values in batch (kind+name+version).
6. `tx.commit()?` → return `IngestReport { run_id, packages: unique_package_count, documents: batch.documents.len(), artifacts: batch.artifacts.len() }`.
7. On ANY error before commit: drop/rollback the transaction AND best-effort remove every path in `created_files` (`let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);` — never panic on cleanup failure), then return the error. The transaction must not commit.
- Prepared statements: use `tx.prepare_cached` where convenient; remember rusqlite `Transaction` borrows the connection mutably — do all file I/O outside the transaction's statement lifetimes (file I/O needs no connection, so sequence statements and file ops; drop statements before calling `tx.commit()`).
- Upsert patterns (return row id via `RETURNING id`):
 - packages: `INSERT INTO packages (kind,name,version,root,first_seen_at,last_seen_at) VALUES (?1,?2,?3,?4,?5,?5) ON CONFLICT(kind, name, COALESCE(version,'')) DO UPDATE SET root=excluded.root, last_seen_at=excluded.last_seen_at RETURNING id`
 - sources: `INSERT INTO sources (provider,source) VALUES (?1,?2) ON CONFLICT(provider,source) DO UPDATE SET provider=excluded.provider RETURNING id`
 - checksums: `INSERT INTO checksums (algorithm,value,size,ref_count) VALUES ('sha256',?1,?2,1) ON CONFLICT(algorithm,value) DO UPDATE SET ref_count=ref_count+1 RETURNING id`
 - documents: `INSERT INTO documents (package_id,source_id,title,relative_path,fs_path,vault_path,origin_url,mime_type,language,size,metadata_checksum,content_checksum_id,content_stored,modified_at,ingested_at) VALUES (?1..?15) ON CONFLICT(package_id, source_id, relative_path) DO UPDATE SET title=excluded.title, fs_path=excluded.fs_path, vault_path=excluded.vault_path, origin_url=excluded.origin_url, mime_type=excluded.mime_type, language=excluded.language, size=excluded.size, metadata_checksum=excluded.metadata_checksum, content_checksum_id=excluded.content_checksum_id, content_stored=excluded.content_stored, modified_at=excluded.modified_at, ingested_at=excluded.ingested_at RETURNING id`
 - artifacts: analogous with `ON CONFLICT(package_id, name, path) DO UPDATE SET ... RETURNING id`
 - tags: `INSERT INTO tags (name) VALUES (?1) ON CONFLICT(name) DO UPDATE SET name=excluded.name RETURNING id`
 - document_tags: `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO document_tags (document_id, tag_id) VALUES (?1,?2)`
 - ingest_runs: plain `INSERT INTO ingest_runs (...) VALUES (...)` + `last_insert_rowid()` or `RETURNING id`.
- NOTE: `ON CONFLICT(kind, name, COALESCE(version,''))` requires the expression index from the schema to exist (it does). If rusqlite/SQLite rejects the expression conflict target, fall back to: upsert by (kind,name,version) for versioned rows AND a second path for NULL-version rows — but try the expression form first; it is supported on the bundled SQLite.

### counts()
`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM packages;` / documents / artifacts → `Counts { ... }` (i64s).

### storage_size()
`SELECT COALESCE(SUM(c.size), 0) FROM checksums c INNER JOIN documents d ON d.content_checksum_id = c.id WHERE d.content_stored = 1;` — i64 result; convert to u64 with `u64::try_from(...).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)` (repo pattern for cast lints).

### verify(layout) — read-only, all categories are warnings
1. `missing_files`: `SELECT fs_path FROM documents WHERE fs_path IS NOT NULL;` → for each, if the path does not exist → push (PathBuf).
2. Stored docs: `SELECT d.vault_path, c.value FROM documents d JOIN checksums c ON d.content_checksum_id = c.id WHERE d.content_stored = 1;` → `checksum_mismatches`: for each, `file = layout.document_file(sha)` where `sha` = vault_path after stripping the `documents/` prefix (or parse from `c.value` — the checksum IS the filename); if the file exists and `content_checksum_file(&file)?` != `c.value` → push file. If the file exists but is a directory or unreadable → treat as mismatch (push it). `orphaned_rows`: if the file does NOT exist → push the vault_path String.
3. `reverse_orphans`: `std::fs::read_dir(layout.documents_dir())` (tolerate NotFound → empty): for each entry, if its file name is not in the set of known stored checksum values (from step 2) → push its path.
4. Sort all four vecs (deterministic output). Return `VerifyReport`.

/// Normalizes and deduplicates collected docs into one batch ready to persist.
/// Documents are keyed by (package, provider, source tag, relative path); the
/// first occurrence wins. Content documents get a SHA-256 content checksum and
/// a logical vault path; metadata-only documents carry neither.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`StorageError`] if a document's content cannot be checksummed
/// (cannot happen in practice: content is in memory) — errors are reserved for
/// future streaming paths.
pub fn normalize_batch(
 layout: &VaultLayout,
 entries: &[(PackageId, CollectedDocs)],
) -> Result<PendingBatch>

/// Ingests collected docs into the vault backend in ONE atomic transaction.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`StorageError`] if normalization or the backend ingest fails
/// (backend rolls back completely on failure).
pub fn ingest_collected(
 layout: &VaultLayout,
 backend: &mut dyn StorageBackend,
 entries: &[(PackageId, CollectedDocs)],
) -> Result<IngestReport>

/// Scans a project directory, collects knowledge from all registered
/// providers, and ingests everything into the vault.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`StorageError`] if the project cannot be detected, a provider
/// collection fails, or the ingest fails.
pub fn ingest_project(
 layout: &VaultLayout,
 backend: &mut dyn StorageBackend,
 root: &Path,
 exclusions: &[String],
) -> Result<IngestReport>
```

## What this is
DKV (Dev Knowledge Vault): an offline-first developer knowledge platform, implemented as a Rust CLI. Not an AI project — AI/RAG is out of scope until every other phase is complete.
Status: Phase 1 (project understanding) partially implemented. Do not redesign or rename modules; extend what exists. The plan's later modules (`providers/`, `scanner/`, `storage/`, `index/`, `search/`) do not exist yet — create them under `src/` when their phase starts.
## Toolchain
- Rust edition 2024, `rust-version = 1.97.1` (that toolchain is installed; build with >= 1.97.1). - Single crate `dkv` with a lib (`src/lib.rs`) and a thin bin (`src/main.rs` dispatching into `dkv::commands`). - Strict lints live in `[lints]` of `Cargo.toml`: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`, clippy all/pedantic/ nursery deny, `unwrap_used`/`expect_used`/`panic`/`todo` deny. Write code compatible with these (prefer `?`, `ok_or_else`, `map_err`).
## Quality gates — end of every milestone, in order
```bash cargo fmt --check cargo check cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings cargo test cargo doc --no-deps ```
All five gates are currently clean (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo doc --no-deps`). Keep them green when touching code.
## Architecture
``` src/ cli.rs # clap definitions (bin-only) main.rs # dispatch + tracing init (-v/-vv/-vvv, --quiet are global) lib.rs # pub mods; exports DkvError, Result, VERSION, APP_NAME commands/ # one module per CLI command config/ # load/save/init of ~/.config/dkv/config.toml (XDG via `directories`) error.rs # DkvError + Result (thiserror) project/ # manifest parsing + detection (cargo.rs, npm.rs, detect.rs) scanner/ # filesystem traversal + `.gitignore`/`.dkvignore` exclusions (mod.rs, ignore.rs) types/ # shared data structures (Config, Dependency, ProjectManifest) util/ # shared utilities (empty stubs) ```
- The spec says `utils/`; the repo uses `util/` (singular). Keep `util/`. - `project/` only understands projects (parsing/detection). It must never download documentation. - `detect.rs` delegates traversal to `src/scanner/`, which reads `.gitignore` / `.dkvignore` and applies config exclusions. Excluded directories (e.g. `target/`, `node_modules/`, `.git`) are pruned from the walk, so detection no longer descends into build-artifact dirs.
## CLI state (real vs stub)
- Implemented: `init` (writes default config), `scan` (prints detected languages/frameworks/packages). - Stubs printing placeholder text in `main.rs`: `sync`, `deps`, `search`, `open`, `update`, `doctor`, `stats`. - `Commands::Scan` takes `SyncArgs`; `ScanArgs` (`cli.rs:101`) is dead code. Harmonize when touching `cli.rs`. - `project/bun.rs` is an empty, unregistered stub — no phase owns it yet.
## Dependencies
Used: anyhow, clap, directories, owo-colors, serde, serde_json, serde_yaml (error.rs only), thiserror, toml, tracing, tracing-subscriber, walkdir. Declared but unused (planned for later phases): cargo_metadata, semver, toml_edit. Dev: tempfile. Spec rule: avoid unnecessary dependencies — only add a dep when the current milestone actually needs it.
## Testing
No tests exist yet; `tests/` does not exist. Fixtures belong under `tests/fixtures/` (spec requires workspace-detection fixtures). Use `tempfile` for scratch dirs.
## Workflow rules (from the project spec)
- Complete one milestone, run all five gates, then STOP and wait for review. Never chain milestones. - Never rewrite working modules, introduce breaking changes, rename public APIs, create duplicate types, move files, or swap the architecture without explicit instruction. - Every public item gets rustdoc; every `Result`-returning fn gets a `# Errors` section. - Milestone deliverable: summary, files created/modified, public API changes, tests added, remaining work, exact commands executed, verification results.
## Repo hygiene
- `.gitignore` only lists `/target`. Don't commit untracked `repomix-output.xml` (regenerate via `repomix`; config: `repomix.config.json`) or `test.txt` (stray `dkv scan` debug output). - No git remotes; work happens on feature branches (currently `feature/milestone-2-config`). - Config quirk: default vault path is the literal string `~/Documents/DevKnowledgeVault` — `~` is never expanded anywhere.use serde::Deserialize;
